scene tsuneyodontpry1
: Oh. Hey, Tsuneyo.
: Hello.
: What are you doing outside of the store?
: I believe they call it “standing.” This is a word that you should probably know as a disgraced former teacher.
: Yeah, that’s why they don’t keep me around anymore. Too many standard words I just never bothered learning.
: At last, someone has finally learned the truth. That someone is me. I will carry this message to those who need to hear it.
: Really though, why are you out here? Aren’t you normally working around this time?
: Yes.
: Are you going to answer the other question too or do I just need to guess?
scene tsuneyodontpry2
: I have been given what is called a “night off.” But this is a concept I do not understand, so I have decided to just stand and wait.
: You’ve had plenty of nights off before. But I guess you- wait.
: You were given the night off?
scene tsuneyodontpry1
: I apologize if you do not understand that word as well. I will do my best to talk slowly and simply so you are able to follow along.
: I know what “given” means. But isn’t your father the only person with the authority to grant you freedom like this? I thought he was out of commission?
: As did I. But it appears that times have changed. So drastically, in fact, that I must now wait outside of the store while he tends to the customers.
: Well...congrats, I guess. I’m happy for you.
: Why?
: Why...am I happy for you?
: Yes. I didn’t believe happiness was an emotion you were capable of feeling.
: Not for myself. I can feel it for other people, though. I think.
: Strange.
: Guess so. Anyway, did you want to head inside with me? I was planning on getting dinner before aimlessly wandering around again and waiting for some sort of event to trigger.
: No.
: Just...going to wait out here then?
: Yes. Same as you.
: Am I not allowed to go inside while your father is working?
: That is correct.
: Why?
: Because my father does not wish to meet the man who has fucked me so many times. I have failed him as a daughter. It is all your fault.
: He doesn’t know what I look like, though. I can just eat and leave.
: He knows.
: How?
: He knows everything. Even words like “given” and “standing.” It is he who should be teaching a class of juveniles, not you.
: I don’t teach anyone anymore.
scene tsuneyodontpry3
: You never have to begin with.
: Well...do you want to just hang out then? I...can eat when I get home later, I guess.
: I suppose that would be a more valuable use of my time. But know that I will not carry you there if you fall unconscious due to fatigue and/or hunger.
: Works for me. I can’t really say that won’t happen though based on just how many times I have “passed out” here.
: It must be something in the air. I am also feeling the effects of it.
: How long have you been out here exactly?
: Five hours.
: Yeah, I think you might just be feeling the effects of prolonged exposure to the sun more than anything else.
scene tsuneyodontpry1
: Possibly. I must ask though, where do you plan to fuck me this time? Because I have also been told to not leave this half of town, meaning you can not fuck me in your house.

scene black
: Okay. I guess we’ll just walk around the old district then. That’s never backfired in any capacity for me before.
: I accept your fucking proposal. Please stay close so I can protect you from the homeless. They can be quite ravenous in the spring.
: Really? Why?
: There is a hallucinogenic flower here that blooms only when the weather rapidly switches between cold and hot. They grind them up and use them to brush their teeth.
: That’s good. Some woman threw one of her teeth at me here once. Maybe the use of hallucinogens can prevent that from happening again?
: Perhaps. Or perhaps they will capture you and dissect you and bring the remains to Tojo Ramen to be turned into soup. There is only one way to find out.
scene tsuneyodontpry4
Tsuneyo and I do a few laps around the old district before coming to a stop at the overlook I almost threw myself over during one of many strange encounters with Yumi.
I’ve had a lot of time to think about myself since then. To really just stand back and reflect on who I am and what I’m doing with my life.
The problem is, I hate my reflection — so I haven’t been able to get very much done on that front despite the amount of time I’ve spent on it.
That’s probably a strange thing to hear coming from the self-proclaimed “world’s worst narcissist.” But hey, I’m forced to be honest over in this part of town.
And when I get to hang over a railing looking at rays from the toxic sun dyeing the sky an uncomfortable shade of brownish orange, that honesty really has a way of just spewing out uncontrollably.
: It’s hideous, don’t you think?
: The sky? The buildings? The...everything else?
: The everything else, yes.
: Before moving into the dorms, I worried that commuting from here to the newer half of Kumon-mi every day would do strange things to my head considering the constant scenery changes.
: To be fair, you still move between both districts every day to check on your father and run the shop.
: This is true. But there’s a real chance it becomes less true going forward now that he seems to be okay.
: Perhaps my usefulness has finally worn off and I can resign myself to the life and duties of a housewife. But what sort of house would marry a girl? I simply do not know.
: I’m sure there are plenty of houses out there that would love to have you, Tsuneyo. But in the event that there aren’t, I’ll gladly go back to being your husband.
: Thank you for your kind consideration. I will get back to you if I am unable to find anything or anyone else.
: Yeah, I don’t blame you for that at all. I find I’m a better backup plan than someone a person should aspire to be with.

The fire within her burned bright! Brighter than the toxic sun! And as her tongue explored a vicious cave that countless others have dared to venture into, she finally felt free! Cured, even!
Like the voices had been silenced now that they could not use either mouth to scream. And if she stayed like this forever, she would never be forced to hear them again.
